chapter_name: Child and adolescent psychiatry and learning disability
chapter_title: Child and adolescent psychiatry and learning disability

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)?

options.text: It is more prevalent in males
Behaviour should occur in at least two settings
Behaviour should persist for at least 3 months
It has an incidence of around 1% in the UK
About 20% of children with ADHD develop dissocial personality traits

correct_answer.text: Behaviour should persist for at least 3 months

correct_answers.text: Behaviour should persist for at least 3 months

questions.explanation: To diagnose ADHD, the inattention and/or hyperactivity should be present in at least two settings and should persist for at least 6 months.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Ritalin(methylphenidate)?

options.text: Its mechanism of action is by increasing release of dopamine and noradrenaline
It increases appetite and weight
Tolerance to it may develop over time
It enhances growth
Growth suppression may be prevented with drug holidays

correct_answer.text: It increases appetite and weight

correct_answers.text: It increases appetite and weight

questions.explanation: Methylphenidate is used in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and narcolepsy. It increases concentration and decreases impulsivity. Growth suppression is a concerning side-effect, which can be reduced by having 'drug holidays'.

questions.question_text: Conduct disorder includes all of the following, except:

options.text: Cruelty to animals
Aggression to humans
Destruction of property
Theft
Obeying rules

correct_answer.text: Obeying rules

correct_answers.text: Obeying rules

questions.explanation: Conduct disorder includes cruelty to animals, aggression to humans, destruction of property, disregard of rules, deceitfulness and theft.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding oppositional defiant disorder?

options.text: It is more common in girls
Onset is after 1 year of age
Behaviour should be seen in two or more situations
It is characterized by serious violation of societal laws
25% of children with the disorder show no symptoms in later life

correct_answer.text: 25% of children with the disorder show no symptoms in later life

correct_answers.text: 25% of children with the disorder show no symptoms in later life

questions.explanation: Oppositional defiant disorder has onset between 3 and 8 years. It is more common in boys but prevalence is equal in adolescents. Children show negative and hostile behaviour but do not break rules or violate the rights of others.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a pervasive developmental disorder?

options.text: ODD
PDD-NOS
Rett syndrome
Asperger syndrome
Autism

correct_answer.text: ODD

correct_answers.text: ODD

questions.explanation: Pervasive developmental disorders (PDDs) are disorders with deficits in social, communication and behavioural skills. They are usually associated with autism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Asperger syndrome?

options.text: It is more common in males
Depression is a very common feature
Deficits in social, language and behavioural skills present
Family history of autism presents
Schizophrenia is more common in children with Asperger syndrome than in the general population

correct_answer.text: Deficits in social, language and behavioural skills present

correct_answers.text: Deficits in social, language and behavioural skills present

questions.explanation: Asperger syndrome is considered in the same spectrum as autism. One of the main differences is that language skills are not affected in Asperger syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)?

options.text: Learning disability is very rare with ADHD
Children with ADHD are good at task completion
Connor's Assessment Scale is used in ADHD
Cognitive behavioural therapy is not effective
ADHD is seen only in children

correct_answer.text: Connor's Assessment Scale is used in ADHD

correct_answers.text: Connor's Assessment Scale is used in ADHD

questions.explanation: 60% of people with ADHD have learning disability. Because of poor attention spans, they are usually bad at task completion. Cognitive behavioural therapy is found to be effective. ADHD is also seen in teenagers and adults.

questions.question_text: Regarding conduct disorder, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: It is more common in boys than girls
Less than 50% of children with the disorder have severe and persistent antisocial problems
Children with poor parenting and low socioeconomic status have a poor prognosis
Children with the disorder usually have a high IQ
Cognitive behavioural therapy and family therapy are helpful in management

correct_answer.text: Children with the disorder usually have a high IQ

correct_answers.text: Children with the disorder usually have a high IQ

questions.explanation: Children with conduct disorder have low IQ. It is more common in boys. Low cerebrospinal fluid serotonin levels, low IQ and brain injury are biological factors associated with risk of conduct disorder.

questions.question_text: What percentage of autistic children suffer from learning disability?
questions.explanation: 70% of autistic children suffer from mild to moderate learning disability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding autism?

options.text: It is characterized by abnormal social relatedness
Onset of symptoms usually occurs after age 3
Restricted, repetitive and stereotyped behaviour is typical
It is more prevalent in males
One-third of children with autism have increased serum serotonin levels

correct_answer.text: Onset of symptoms usually occurs after age 3

correct_answers.text: Onset of symptoms usually occurs after age 3

questions.explanation: In autism, symptoms usually appear before the age of 3. Autism is characterized by abnormal social relatedness, qualitative abnormality in communication and restricted, repetitive and stereotyped behaviour.

questions.question_text: What percentage of children in the UK have a reading disorder?
questions.explanation: 4% of school-age children have difficulty in reading. A male predominance has been noted.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding enuresis?

options.text: It is more common in females
It is usually diagnosed in the first year of birth
No family history has been noted
Behavioural modification is the mainstay of treatment
It results in high self-esteem

correct_answer.text: Behavioural modification is the mainstay of treatment

correct_answers.text: Behavioural modification is the mainstay of treatment

questions.explanation: Enuresis is micturition in a child of 5 years or more, usually at night. This could be voluntary or involuntary. Usually there is a family history. It is more common in males and results in low self-esteem. Imipramine may be used if behavioural management does not work.

questions.question_text: Concerning Gilles de la Tourette syndrome, which of the following statements is false?

options.text: It is characterized by motor and vocal tics
Its prevalence is around 5 per 10 000
It is usually associated with obsessive compulsive disorder
Psycho-education and cognitive behavioural therapy have been found to be helpful
It does not cause distress or affect functioning

correct_answer.text: It does not cause distress or affect functioning

correct_answers.text: It does not cause distress or affect functioning

questions.explanation: Gilles de la Tourette syndrome is characterized by motor and vocal tics. It causes distress and impaired functioning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding major depression in children?

options.text: Risk of suicide is high
There is a prevalence of up to 3% in prepubescent children
20% of these children later manifest bipolar disorder as adults
It is prevalent more in males in the adolescent age group
Psychotherapy is the treatment of choice

correct_answer.text: It is prevalent more in males in the adolescent age group

correct_answers.text: It is prevalent more in males in the adolescent age group

questions.explanation: Major depression has an equal gender ratio in prepubescent children. However, in adolescent groups prevalence is 8% for males and 14% for females.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of schizophrenia in children?

options.text: There is a better prognosis than in adults
It has a more insidious onset
About 70% later receive a diagnosis of bipolar disorder or schizoaffective disorder
It responds well to treatment
Delusion is the most common symptom

correct_answer.text: It has a more insidious onset

correct_answers.text: It has a more insidious onset

questions.explanation: Schizophrenia in children has a poor prognosis, an insidious onset and responds poorly to treatment. Delusions and catatonia are rare. Only 30% of children receive a diagnosis of schizoaffective disorder or bipolar disorder in later life.

questions.question_text: A 10-year-old boy has been diagnosed as suffering from attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, with no comorbidity. The family have tried psychotherapy and want to know about any pharmacological interventions. Which would be the drug of choice in this condition?

options.text: Imipramine
Fluoxetine
Methylphenidate
Desipramine
Atomoxetine

correct_answer.text: Methylphenidate

correct_answers.text: Methylphenidate

questions.explanation: The drug of choice in ADHD with no comorbidity, according to National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines, is methylphenidate. It has to be started at a low dose and titrated weekly.

questions.question_text: Regarding hyperkinetic disorder, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: It may be diagnosed by a GP
It can be diagnosed through rating scales alone
Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder should be considered in all age groups
It can be diagnosed even if the history shows that it is prevalent only in one setting
Dietary fatty acid supplements are recommended for treatment

correct_answer.text: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder should be considered in all age groups

correct_answers.text: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder should be considered in all age groups

questions.explanation: According to National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines, hyperkinetic disorder should be considered in all age groups. It should be diagnosed by specialists or professionals with appropriate training and expertise. It should not be diagnosed from rating scales or observational data alone. The symptoms should also be present in at least two settings for the diagnosis to be made. Dietary fatty acid supplementation is not recommended.

questions.question_text: National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) recommendations for depression in children include all of the following, except:

options.text: Drugs are not recommended as the first-line treatment in mild depression
Psychotherapy is the first-line treatment for moderate to severe depression
Medication should be offered in combination with psychotherapy
The preferred antidepressant is fluoxetine, after a course of psychotherapy has been tried
A child when initially diagnosed with mild depression should be referred to tier 4 CAMHS

correct_answer.text: A child when initially diagnosed with mild depression should be referred to tier 4 CAMHS

correct_answers.text: A child when initially diagnosed with mild depression should be referred to tier 4 CAMHS

questions.explanation: Refer to National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines on depression in children and young people. Mild depression should be referred to tier 1 in the first instance. No medication is recommended for mild depression.

questions.question_text: What percentage of children and young people suffer from obsessive compulsive disorder?
questions.explanation: About 1% of children and young people suffer from obsessive compulsive disorder, according to National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines.

questions.question_text: A 7-year-old boy has been diagnosed with severe obsessive compulsive disorder, with no comorbidity. Psychotherapy has been tried with not much benefit. The multidisciplinary team has discussed treatment with his family and has agreed on trying pharmacological intervention. Which is the medication of choice according to National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines?

options.text: Fluoxetine
Sertraline
Fluvoxamine
Tricyclics
Methylphenidate

correct_answer.text: Sertraline

correct_answers.text: Sertraline

questions.explanation: Sertraline is the drug of choice according to National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines. Sertraline and fluvoxamine are preferred in obsessive compulsive disorder with no comorbid symptoms. However, fluvoxamine is authorized only in children above 8 years old.

questions.question_text: Which is the drug of choice in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder with conduct disorder?

options.text: Atomoxetine
Risperidone
Methylphenidate
Fluoxetine
Clonidine

correct_answer.text: Methylphenidate

correct_answers.text: Methylphenidate

questions.explanation: The National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) recommends methylphenidate in children with ADHD with conduct disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of atomoxetine?

options.text: It is the drug of choice in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder with no comorbid symptoms according to National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines
It does not have any gastric side-effects
It is a stimulant medication
It works as a noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor
It is not approved for use in adults

correct_answer.text: It works as a noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor

correct_answers.text: It works as a noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor

questions.explanation: Atomoxetine is a noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor used in ADHD. It can be used in children and adults. The most common side-effects include nausea and vomiting.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding autism?

options.text: Age of onset is before 38 months
There is a preponderance in males
Communication difficulties present
It is characterized by lack of friends
Autistic children usually have a high IQ

correct_answer.text: Autistic children usually have a high IQ

correct_answers.text: Autistic children usually have a high IQ

questions.explanation: About 70% of autistic children have low IQ. The male:female ratio is 3–4:1.

questions.question_text: In Rett syndrome, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Prenatal and perinatal development is normal
Head circumference at birth is normal
It is seen only in girls
There is acceleration of head growth between 5 and 48 months
Gait and trunk movements are poorly coordinated

correct_answer.text: There is acceleration of head growth between 5 and 48 months

correct_answers.text: There is acceleration of head growth between 5 and 48 months

questions.explanation: Rett syndrome is seen only in girls. There is normal growth until 5 months, then from 6 months there is deceleration of head growth.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder?

options.text: Being physically cruel to animals
Failure to sustain attention during a task
Leaving one's seat in a classroom when expected to sit down
Blurting out the answer before questions are completed
Talking excessively without appropriate response to social constraints

correct_answer.text: Being physically cruel to animals

correct_answers.text: Being physically cruel to animals

questions.explanation: Cruelty and aggression to animals and people are part of conduct disorder.

questions.question_text: What percentage of learning disability is due to prenatal factors?
questions.explanation: 50–70% of cases are due to prenatal factors, 10–20% to perinatal and another 5–10% to postnatal factors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Down syndrome?

options.text: It is the most common genetic cause of learning disability
It is due to trisomy of chromosome 21
Children with Down syndrome have characteristic facies and habitus
Learning disability is evident before the age of 1 year
IQ in adults is usually less than 50

correct_answer.text: Learning disability is evident before the age of 1 year

correct_answers.text: Learning disability is evident before the age of 1 year

questions.explanation: Although Down syndrome is diagnosed at birth, learning disability becomes evident only by the end of the first year.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding Patau syndrome?

options.text: It is due to trisomy of chromosome 17
Children with the syndrome may have rocker-bottom feet
Children with the syndrome have normal genitalia
IQ is usually normal
It is caused only by non-disjunction of chromosomes during meiosis

correct_answer.text: Children with the syndrome may have rocker-bottom feet

correct_answers.text: Children with the syndrome may have rocker-bottom feet

questions.explanation: Patau syndrome is due to trisomy of chromosome 13. Children with Patau syndrome have abnormal genitalia and low IQ. It can be caused by other malfunctions like translocation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Down syndrome?

options.text: Incidence per 1000 live births increases for women over 35
Raised IgM and IgG levels are features
The usual genetic cause is a Robertsonian translocation
Most children with Down syndrome are born to mothers under the age of 35
About half of people with Down syndrome have congenital heart defects

correct_answer.text: The usual genetic cause is a Robertsonian translocation

correct_answers.text: The usual genetic cause is a Robertsonian translocation

questions.explanation: The most common cause of Down syndrome is trisomy 21 (more than 95% of cases). Only less than 5% is due to a Robertsonian translocation.

questions.question_text: All of the following diseases in the mother during pregnancy can lead to learning disability, except:

options.text: Diabetes
Hypothyroidism
Syphilis
German measles
Measles

correct_answer.text: Measles

correct_answers.text: Measles

questions.explanation: Learning disability in a baby can be caused by the mother suffering from one of the following illnesses: non-infectious causes are diabetes, hypothyroidism, hypertension and malnutrition; infectious causes includes syphilis, HIV and TORCH (toxoplasmosis, rubella, cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex) (rubella is German measles).

questions.question_text: People with Down syndrome have an increased risk of:

options.text: Vascular dementia
Hyperthyroidism
Depression
Hypermetropia
Macrocephaly

correct_answer.text: Depression

correct_answers.text: Depression

questions.explanation: Down syndrome patients have an increased risk of Alzheimer's dementia, hypothyroidism (20%), depression (10%), myopia (30%) and brachycephaly.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of Down syndrome?

options.text: High-arched palate
Short stature
Protruding tongue
Kayser–Fleischer ring
Simian crease

correct_answer.text: Kayser–Fleischer ring

correct_answers.text: Kayser–Fleischer ring

questions.explanation: Kayser–Fleischer rings are dark rings that are seen around the iris in copper poisoning. The eye manifestation seen in Down syndrome is Brushfield spots, which are grey or very light yellow spots on the iris.

questions.question_text: With which of the following syndromes is learning disability rarely associated?

options.text: Down syndrome
Turner syndrome
Trisomy X
Klinefelter syndrome
XYY male

correct_answer.text: Turner syndrome

correct_answers.text: Turner syndrome

questions.explanation: Turner syndrome does not typically cause learning disability. Males with XYY may have slightly lower than average IQ.

questions.question_text: Prader–Willi syndrome consists of all of the following, except:

options.text: Acromicria
Hypogenitalism
Tall stature
Mild to moderate learning disability
Obesity

correct_answer.text: Tall stature

correct_answers.text: Tall stature

questions.explanation: Features of Prader–Willi syndrome include short stature, hypogenitalism (cryptorchidism, micropenis, amenorrhoea), overeating, obesity, mild to moderate learning disability and sleep disorders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of Angelman syndrome?

options.text: Paroxysms of crying
Micrognathia
Epilepsy
Normal IQ
Macrocephaly

correct_answer.text: Epilepsy

correct_answers.text: Epilepsy

questions.explanation: Angelman (happy puppet) syndrome features ataxia, epilepsy (86%), paroxysms of laughter, microcephaly, seizures and abnormal EEG.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding phenylketonuria?

options.text: It is an unpreventable cause of learning disability
It can be detected by the Widal test
It can be treated by external supply of phenylalanine
It is caused by a defect on the short arm of chromosome 12
Behaviour symptoms include temper tantrums and hyperactivity

correct_answer.text: Behaviour symptoms include temper tantrums and hyperactivity

correct_answers.text: Behaviour symptoms include temper tantrums and hyperactivity

questions.explanation: Phenylketonuria is a preventable cause of learning disability. It is due to deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase. The gene for phenylalanine hydroxylase is located on the long arm of chromosome 12. It is detected postnatally by the Guthrie test. Management consists of restriction of phenylalanine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding fragile X syndrome?

options.text: It shows a triplet sequence of CCG
It is transmitted as X-linked recessive
It does not occur in females
It is the most common inherited cause of learning disability
It has very high penetrance

correct_answer.text: It is the most common inherited cause of learning disability

correct_answers.text: It is the most common inherited cause of learning disability

questions.explanation: Fragile X syndrome is the most common inherited cause of learning disability. It has low penetrance. It can occur in both sexes. It is an X-linked dominant condition and shows a repeat of the CGG nucleotide.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is associated with tall stature?

options.text: Down syndrome
XYY
Foetal alcohol syndrome
Prader–Willi syndrome
Hunter syndrome

correct_answer.text: XYY

correct_answers.text: XYY

questions.explanation: All are associated with short stature except XYY. Other syndromes that feature tall stature are XXY and fragile X.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is associated with microcephaly?

options.text: Down syndrome
Cri-du-chat
Hurler syndrome
Hydrocephalus
Fragile X

correct_answer.text: Cri-du-chat

correct_answers.text: Cri-du-chat

questions.explanation: Cri-du-chat syndrome is caused by a deletion on chromosome 5. It is usually sporadic. It causes a cat-like cry, microcephaly and a rounded face. It is usually associated with severe or profound learning disability.

questions.question_text: The clinical picture of congenital hypothyroidism includes all of the following, except:

options.text: Hyperactivity
Feeding difficulty
Constipation
Macroglossia
Umbilical hernia

correct_answer.text: Hyperactivity

correct_answers.text: Hyperactivity

questions.explanation: Congenital hypothyroidism is a treatable cause of mental and growth retardation. The typical clinical picture in an untreated case is one of lethargy, feeding difficulty, constipation, macroglossia and umbilical hernia.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following disorders would benefit from dietary restriction?

options.text: Down syndrome
Sturge–Weber syndrome
Phenylketonuria
Hunter syndrome
Fragile X syndrome

correct_answer.text: Phenylketonuria

correct_answers.text: Phenylketonuria

questions.explanation: Dietary restriction of phenylalanine may improve prognosis in phenylketonuria.

questions.question_text: What is the prevalence of epilepsy in hospitalized patients with learning disability?
questions.explanation: The prevalence of epilepsy in the hospitalized learning-disabled population is 40%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding psychiatric diseases in individuals with learning disability?

options.text: Age of onset of schizophrenia tends to be earlier than in the general population
Genetic factors are important in the aetiology of schizophrenia
Bipolar disorder is less prevalent than in the general population
Suicidal thoughts are less frequent in individuals with severe learning disability than in those with mild/moderate learning disability
Anxiety disorders are difficult to differentiate from depression

correct_answer.text: Bipolar disorder is less prevalent than in the general population

correct_answers.text: Bipolar disorder is less prevalent than in the general population

questions.explanation: The age of onset of schizophrenia tends to be earlier in learning disability than in the general population (mean 23 years). Mood disorders are more prevalent in learning disability, but suicidal thoughts may be less prevalent in the severely disabled. It is usually difficult to differentiate anxiety disorders from depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding behaviour disorders in individuals with learning disability?

options.text: Self-injurious behaviour is less common in severe learning disability
'Self-hugging' stereotypic behaviour is seen in Lesch–Nyhan syndrome
In Smith–Magenis syndrome clients show a hand-flapping stereotype
Behavioural disorder prevalence is around 7% of the population with learning disability
Behavioural disorders are less prevalent in inpatients than in the community

correct_answer.text: Behavioural disorder prevalence is around 7% of the population with learning disability

correct_answers.text: Behavioural disorder prevalence is around 7% of the population with learning disability

questions.explanation: Self-injurious behaviour is more common with severe learning disability. Behavioural disorders are more prevalent (two to three times) in inpatients than in the community. Learning-disabled patients with genetic aetiology may have characteristic behaviour stereotypes. In Smith–Magenis syndrome, they show 'self-hugging' behaviour. Hand-flapping is seen in fragile X syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding the DSM-IV classification of mental retardation?

options.text: Adults with mild mental retardation can live independently with appropriate support and raise their own families
Moderate mental retardation is the most frequent type of mental retardation
Children with profound mental retardation may be taught some self-care skills
Most children with moderate mental retardation acquire language and can communicate adequately during early childhood
The cause of severe mental retardation is more likely to be identified than the causes of other milder forms

correct_answer.text: Moderate mental retardation is the most frequent type of mental retardation

correct_answers.text: Moderate mental retardation is the most frequent type of mental retardation

questions.explanation: Mild mental retardation is the most frequent type of mental retardation (85%). Many adults can live independently with appropriate support and raise their own families. Moderate mental retardation is the second most prevalent (10%). People with moderate mental retardation acquire knowledge and can communicate adequately during early childhood. Severe mental retardation occurs in 4% and the cause of the mental retardation can be identified more readily than in milder cases. Such people may adapt well to supervised living situations such as group homes and also manage to perform work-related tasks under supervision. Profoundly mentally retarded persons represent around 1–2%. They may be taught some self-care skills and learn to communicate their needs given the appropriate training.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding children with Smith–Magenis syndrome?

options.text: They usually have mild mental retardation
They present with self-injury behaviour like head-banging and hand-biting
They have decreased REM sleep
Their voice is usually hoarse and deep
The syndrome is caused by complete or partial deletion of 17p11

correct_answer.text: They usually have mild mental retardation

correct_answers.text: They usually have mild mental retardation

questions.explanation: Smith–Magenis syndrome presents with severe mental retardation. The syndrome is caused by complete or partial deletion of 17p11. People with Smith–Magenis syndrome show hyperactivity and self-injury behaviour and their voice is deep and hoarse.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding tuberous sclerosis?

options.text: It is an autosomal-recessive condition
More than 80% of patients have learning disability
The cancerous growths seen are known as hamartomas
It is caused by deletion on chromosome 5
There may be associated developmental delay

correct_answer.text: There may be associated developmental delay

correct_answers.text: There may be associated developmental delay

questions.explanation: Tuberous sclerosis is an autosomal-dominant condition with 100% penetrance. It is a multisystemic genetic disease with two genetic loci, on chromosomes 9 and 16. Around 50% suffer from learning disability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding Angelman syndrome?

options.text: It usually presents with macrocephaly
It is named after the first patient diagnosed with the syndrome
Speech development is normal
Characteristic patterns are seen on EEG
It is caused by inactivation of paternally inherited chromosome 15

correct_answer.text: Characteristic patterns are seen on EEG

correct_answers.text: Characteristic patterns are seen on EEG

questions.explanation: Angelman syndrome is named after Dr Harry Angelman, the British doctor who first described the illness. It is caused by deletion of the maternally inherited chromosome 15. Usual presentation includes developmental delay, speech impairment, ataxia and repetitive behaviour. Other common features include microcephaly, seizures and abnormal EEG.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Folic-acid supplementation during early pregnancy reduces the prevalence of learning disability
Maternal illnesses like diabetes can lead to learning disability
Urinary tract infection (UTI) in the mother during pregnancy leads to learning disability in the child
Neonatal screening for hypothyroidism prevents learning disability
Central nervous system infections in the first year of life can lead to learning disability

correct_answer.text: Urinary tract infection (UTI) in the mother during pregnancy leads to learning disability in the child

correct_answers.text: Urinary tract infection (UTI) in the mother during pregnancy leads to learning disability in the child

questions.explanation: Folic-acid supplementation reduces learning disability. The mother having a UTI during pregnancy has not been seen to cause learning disability in the baby.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Rett syndrome?

options.text: Symptoms can be seen from the first month of life
It exclusively affects girls
It is often associated with autism
Self-injury presents in 40–50% of patients
Epilepsy is a common feature

correct_answer.text: Symptoms can be seen from the first month of life

correct_answers.text: Symptoms can be seen from the first month of life

questions.explanation: Rett syndrome is exclusively seen in girls; development is normal until 18–24 months. Associated features include autism, epilepsy and abnormal involuntary movement. Behavioural symptoms include low mood, anxiety and self-injury.
